questions.def: 'Whose' indicates possession by the author.
questions.question: The author, ___ research is groundbreaking, won the award.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces a non-restrictive relative clause about the report.
questions.question: The report, ___ was published last week, is already outdated.

questions.def: The noun 'advocate' fits as the subject's description.
questions.question: He is an ___ of sustainable energy.

questions.def: 'In which' is a formal way to introduce a relative clause of place.
questions.question: The city ___ I grew up is very different now.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession: the essay belongs to the student.
questions.question: The student, ___ essay was praised, felt encouraged.

questions.def: Past participle 'deemed' is needed after 'was' for passive voice.
questions.question: The document was ___ confidential.

questions.def: Elliptical relative clause. Equivalent to: the implications of which...
questions.question: The theory, ___ implications are far-reaching, is still debated.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces a non-restrictive relative clause.
questions.question: The results, ___ were unexpected, led to new research.

questions.def: 'Cited' (past participle) acts as an adjective modifying research.
questions.question: The ___ research supports the claim.

questions.def: 'Which' correctly replaces 'the conference' as the object.
questions.question: The conference, ___ I attended, was very informative.

questions.def: 'That' is used for restrictive relative clauses referring to things.
questions.question: This is the book ___ I was telling you about.

questions.def: 'Clarified' acts as an adjective, indicating the explanation was made clearer.
questions.question: The ___ explanation helped.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession: the roof belongs to the house.
questions.question: The house, ___ roof was damaged, needed repair.

questions.def: 'Of which' correctly refers back to the project.
questions.question: The project, the success ___ was crucial, proceeded well.

questions.def: 'Demonstrated' acts as an adjective indicating what kind of technology.
questions.question: The ___ technology is innovative.

questions.def: 'On which' introduces a relative clause referring to the principle.
questions.question: The principle ___ the argument is based is flawed.

questions.def: 'Whose' indicates possession: the architect belongs to the building.
questions.question: The building ___ architect is famous, is a landmark.

questions.def: 'Analysed' acts as an adjective. The data has been analysed.
questions.question: The ___ data revealed patterns.

questions.def: 'Whom' is the object of the verb 'admire'.
questions.question: He is the professor ___ students admire greatly.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces a non-restrictive relative clause.
questions.question: The essay, ___ I submitted yesterday, received good feedback.

questions.def: 'Investigated' is a past participle used as an adjective.
questions.question: The ___ claim turned out to be true.

questions.def: 'Of which' is the correct form to use in this context.
questions.question: The argument, the validity ___ is questionable, is complex.

questions.def: 'Of which' indicates the relationship between law and purpose.
questions.question: The law, the purpose ___ is to protect citizens, is important.

questions.def: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun, showing the author possesses the work.
questions.question: The author, ___ work I admire, will speak tonight.

questions.def: 'The' is a definite article required before 'implications' in this restrictive clause.
questions.question: The policy, ___ implications are far-reaching, was approved.

questions.def: 'Written' is a past participle forming a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The report, ___ by the committee, is now public.

questions.def: 'Whose' indicates possession, connecting the scientist to their discoveries.
questions.question: The scientist, ___ discoveries revolutionized the field, retired.

questions.def: 'By which' correctly introduces a relative clause specifying the means.
questions.question: This is the method ___ we arrived at the solution.

questions.def: Non-restrictive clauses need 'which,' not 'that,' after a comma.
questions.question: The house, that was built in 1920, is now for sale.

questions.def: 'Published' is the past participle, forming a reduced relative clause.
questions.question: The article, ___ in the journal, is highly influential.
